# Glint Indexer 2.4 deployment guide

## Release summary

Glint Indexer 2.4 replaces the in-memory batch scheduler while retaining the version-3 segment format used by 2.3. This guide covers an upgrade from 2.3 to 2.4. Mixed worker versions are supported during deployment, and existing segments need no rewrite, export, or format conversion. There is no protocol change or client-side configuration migration.

Deploy one canary worker, evaluate ten complete one-minute samples, and then promote to the remaining workers. Keep ordinary ingest enabled throughout a healthy rollout. The same controller provides rollback to the captured 2.3 deployment if an observed metric breaches its threshold.

## Establish the starting state

Use `glintctl` version 2.4 for these commands. Before changing any worker, inspect the target cluster:

```sh
glintctl cluster inspect --cluster production
```

Confirm that the coordinator is already at version 5.8 or later, all starting workers are on 2.3, and at least four workers report ready. The minimum ready count allows one worker to serve as the canary while the others remain on the previous version. Record the coordinator version for the release record.

Prepare `worker-2.4.yaml` with `drain_timeout_seconds` set to at least 45. This is the supported checkpoint-drain window for the rollout. Validate the prepared configuration:

```sh
glintctl config validate --file worker-2.4.yaml
```

Resolve validation errors before applying the configuration and record the successful result. Validation checks the file; it does not deploy a worker. Keeping these steps separate gives the release owner a verified configuration before the first replacement begins.

## Start the single-worker canary

Begin with exactly one upgraded worker:

```sh
glintctl rollout start --cluster production --version 2.4 --config worker-2.4.yaml --canary-workers 1
```

The rollout controller drains the selected worker to its last committed checkpoint before replacing it. The other workers remain available on 2.3 during this initial stage. Ordinary ingest stays enabled; movement in queue age alone is not a reason to pause it.

Check readiness and rollout phase:

```sh
glintctl rollout status --cluster production
```

This status reports canary readiness and active worker versions. Record the canary ready time. Do not begin its observation window before readiness is reported, and do not promote a canary that has not reached that state. Readiness establishes the start of measurement, rather than permission to upgrade the rest of the cluster immediately.

## Evaluate the canary window

Collect the cluster-wide metrics once per minute:

```sh
glintctl metrics watch --cluster production --interval 60s
```

Start a sequence of ten consecutive complete samples after the canary is ready. For every sample, evaluate both of these limits:

| Metric | Unit | Passing value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `commit_error_ratio` | Unitless ratio | At most 0.002. |
| `oldest_pending_age_seconds` | Seconds | At most 90. |

A value exactly on either threshold passes. Both metrics describe the cluster, not only the canary worker. Record each pair of values so the promotion decision can be reconstructed from the observations. A smoothed dashboard average is not a substitute for the individual samples.

Read the ratio in its stated unit: 0.002 is 0.2%, not 2%. For example, a sample with `commit_error_ratio` of 0.001 and queue age of 91 seconds fails because the queue-age limit is exceeded. A sample with a ratio of 0.002 and queue age of 90 seconds passes both limits. These are per-sample decisions. The first example still requires rollback even if the next nine samples have lower queue ages; those later observations do not erase the observed breach.

Every sample must pass both limits. Any observed threshold breach requires rollback, even if later values would bring an average below the threshold. A missing sample means the window is incomplete: collect a fresh sequence of ten consecutive complete samples before deciding to promote. Missing data alone does not trigger rollback, but it also cannot count as a passing minute.

## Promote and verify the fleet

After a complete passing canary window, continue the rollout:

```sh
glintctl rollout promote --cluster production
```

Promotion replaces the remaining workers one at a time. Continue watching the same cluster-wide thresholds while those replacements proceed. A breach during promotion follows the rollback procedure just as a breach during the canary does; passing the initial window does not suspend the limits.

Use rollout status to confirm that every worker reports version 2.4 and the rollout phase reports `complete`. These are the deployment completion conditions. The earlier canary result proves only that promotion was justified at that point; it does not prove the whole fleet has finished upgrading.

After completion, collect ten additional consecutive complete one-minute samples meeting the same thresholds. A missing sample restarts this observation window, and a threshold breach requires rollback. Close the release only after this final sequence passes. Record final worker versions and the completion observations alongside the original canary evidence.

## Roll back a breached rollout

Use the controller to restore the captured 2.3 deployment:

```sh
glintctl rollout rollback --cluster production --version 2.3
```

Rollback restores the worker binary and configuration captured when the rollout started. The controller drains workers, preserves committed segments, and replays uncommitted batches from the last committed checkpoint. The unchanged version-3 format allows 2.3 to read existing segments after restoration.

Keep ingest enabled during rollback. Do not delete segments or reset the ingest offset: neither action is part of restoring the previous worker deployment, and the controller already handles replay from the committed checkpoint.

Check that every worker reports version 2.3. Then require `oldest_pending_age_seconds` to remain at most 90 for five consecutive complete one-minute samples. Missing samples restart that five-sample sequence. Rollback is operationally complete only when both the worker-version check and this queue-age observation pass.

## Close the release record

Capture the coordinator version, configuration validation result, canary ready time, and all ten canary sample pairs. Add the promotion or rollback decision, final worker versions, and the completion samples applicable to that path. For a promoted release, those are the ten post-completion metric pairs; for rollback, they are the five queue-age samples.

The record connects each decision to its evidence: readiness starts observation, complete passing samples permit promotion, fleet status establishes deployment completion, and the final observation sequence permits closure.

A missing canary sample requires a fresh sequence of ten consecutive complete samples.
Promotion replaces the remaining workers one at a time.
A promoted release requires ten additional passing one-minute samples after deployment completion before closure.
